movie.title: HIM
movie.overview: After suffering a potentially career-ending brain trauma, Cameron Cade receives a lifeline when his hero, legendary eight-time Championship quarterback and cultural megastar Isaiah White, offers to train Cam at Isaiah's isolated compound that he shares with his celebrity influencer wife. But as Cam's training accelerates, Isaiah's charisma begins to curdle into something darker.

reviews.author: Brent Marchant
reviews.content: Producer-writer-director Jordan Peele has quickly developed quite a reputation for making horror flicks/psychological thrillers that undeniably push the envelope of these genres, turning out creations unlike anything most moviegoers have ever seen. In the process, he has often packed his pictures with much for viewers to process on multiple levels as they walk out of the theater. And, in his latest offering, in which Peele has acted as producer, handing over the writing and directing responsibilities to filmmaker Justin Tipping, he has overseen the birth of yet another release in the same vein as previous projects like “Get Out” (2017), “Us” (2019) and “Nope” (2022) – only this time on steroids and laced with a touch of crack. “Him” tells the story of Cameron Cade (Tyriq Withers), a pro football prospect who’s looked upon by many as the sport’s next quarterback G.O.A.T. (i.e., “greatest of all time”). His future looks bright until he experiences a baffling yet devastating head injury at the hands of disturbed fan teetering on the edge of sanity. So, in an effort to reinvigorate his skills (and to rejuvenate his career), he agrees to be taken under the wing of veteran hurler Isaiah White (Marlon Wayans), a QB who led his team to eight championships but is now on the fence about retirement. When the recovering protégé begins his mentorship under the sports legend, however, he gets much more than he bargained for. He enters a world in which he becomes ensconced in a dizzying mix of hyper-ambition, psychological gamesmanship, professional jealousy and an aberrant culture that gleefully and relentlessly celebrates mind-numbing brutality. Given Cam’s precarious mental state in the wake of his injury, combined with an onslaught of conflicting messages, mind games and bizarre occurrences that straddle the borders of reality, he struggles to make sense of it all, particularly when it comes to deciding whether to embrace or abandon the world of which he’s about to become a part. His existence turns surreal, confusing, and, above all, troubling. He has some big decisions to make, provided if he’s even capable of thinking straight at this point. But the film is about more than just Cam’s struggle to hold on to his sanity in the face of his mentor’s malevolence, gaslighting and questionable motives; it’s also a strong statement about the bloodsport culture of football and the ways in which society has come to worship it as something akin to a perverse religious cult. In fact, the narrative is riddled with ominous Biblical and Satanic symbolism, elements that have been suitably tweaked to reflect the nature of the world of pro football and the exalted position it’s been accorded in contemporary society. Yet, curiously enough, in making its case, the film tells a tale that alternates between being deadly serious with its troubling imagery and not taking itself seriously at all with its astutely timed sinister comic relief, walking a precarious tightrope of moods that keeps viewers guessing about what’s really going on here. In the process, it provides a perfect showcase for Wayans to show off acting chops that most of us probably never knew he possessed; his ability to switch gears and turn on a dime and make it look effortless is truly impressive. Add to those qualities the film’s breakneck pacing, edgy film editing, stunning visuals and eclectic production design, and you’ve got a cinematic rollercoaster that’s sure to leave you exhilarated, exhausted and unnerved by the time the credits roll. Now, this is not to suggest that the film is without problems. The narrative is excessively overstuffed and somewhat unfocused at times (no doubt to try and convey what it’s like to be in Cam’s head under these circumstances), and its various messages can be more than a little obvious and heavy-handed on occasion. However, even if “Him” is not perfect, Tipping and Peele should be commended for trying to breathe new life into a genre that’s been releasing a steady stream of lame, half-baked offerings of late, and I’ll take this offering over any of its underwhelming wannabe peers any day of the week.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: We start off watching a young lad glued to the television where his American footballing idol “Isaiah” (Marlon Wayans) is out to set some records. An injury ensues during that game before we spool on until the young lad himself is now a budding superstar (Tyriq Withers) and after he’s been rather brutally thwacked on the head and suffered some brain swelling, his hero invites him to train at his underground desert compound where it becomes very clear that not only did he recover, mysteriously, from his on-field injury many years earlier but that he went on to become a legend of his sport. “Cam” is completely phased by his new opportunity but once he has met his idol, his rather bizarre wife and their enigmatic physician-cum-trainer he becomes increasingly aware that there are more than just the obvious ice baths and sacrifices to be made. Originally, I thought there might be an element of the horror to this. Maybe something along the lines of that Charlie Daniels song? Then I thought it was just an excuse for attractive men to glisten up with sweat and wrestle about on the floor? Then I thought I’d forgotten to buy milk - and that’s when I realised that I had no idea what I was watching, nor why. Sure, we get the usual work hard to play hard vibe as well a sense of the dedication and perseverance needed to thrive, but there’s neither much of a plot nor any character development and once you’ve seen Withers in a towel for the tenth time, even that begins to wear (but not come) off. This is a really disappointingly self indulgent piece of cinema that culminates ridiculously and left me cold. Perhaps I just wasn’t in the right mood, but I thought this a waste of ninety minutes.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When a promising young athlete recovering from a severe brain injury joins his legendary football idol at a remote training compound, he discovers that his hero's intense mentorship hides a dark, chilling sinister agenda.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: After suffering a potentially career-ending brain trauma, aspiring quarterback Cameron Cade accepts a once-in-a-lifetime offer to train at the isolated estate of his idol, eight-time champion Isaiah White. Surrounded by the opulent yet unsettling lifestyle Isaiah shares with his influencer wife, Cam pushes his physical and mental limits to achieve greatness. However, as the rigorous regimen intensifies, Isaiah's magnetic charisma twists into psychological manipulation and terrifying control. Cam is forced to confront the sinister reality behind his hero's legendary success before his own mind and life are permanently destroyed.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Cameron Cade is a gifted young football prospect whose rising career hits a devastating standstill following a horrific brain injury on the field. Desperate to rebuild his future, Cam receives an unexpected lifeline from Isaiah White, a legendary eight-time championship quarterback and global cultural icon. Isaiah invites Cam to his ultra-exclusive, secluded compound to personally mentor him back to peak performance. Upon arrival, Cam is immersed in a high-tech, luxurious environment shared by Isaiah and his glamorous influencer wife, both of whom project an image of perfection. Initial training sessions yield astonishing physical progress, restoring Cam's confidence and instilling absolute devotion to his mentor. As time passes, however, the isolated nature of the compound begins to weigh heavily on Cam, cutting him off from the outside world. Isaiah's motivational tactics grow increasingly aggressive, crossing the line from intense coaching into psychological torture and surreal torment. Cam begins experiencing horrifying hallucinations and unsettling lapses in memory, uncertain if they stem from his prior trauma or something far more nefarious occurring at the facility. Terrifying clues suggest that Isaiah's unmatched legacy is built on horrific sacrifices, forcing Cam into a desperate struggle to escape the compound with his life and sanity intact.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: HIM is a psychological horror thriller that explores the dark obsession with athletic perfection, celebrity worship, and the predatory nature of toxic mentorship. The story centers on Cameron Cade, a brilliant high school quarterback whose promising future is shattered by a devastating head injury. Facing the abrupt end of his athletic dreams, Cam is unexpectedly thrown a lifeline by Isaiah White, an eight-time championship quarterback widely regarded as the greatest athlete of his generation. Isaiah invites Cam to his deeply isolated, high-tech compound—a private paradise he shares with his famous influencer wife—promising to restore Cam's mind and body through a revolutionary, highly secret training regimen. Isolated from his family, friends, and the media, Cam throws himself into the demanding program, initially experiencing miraculous physical gains under the guidance of his childhood hero. But as the compound's walls feel increasingly like a cage, the atmosphere transforms from inspiring to deeply oppressive. Isaiah's charismatic persona starts to fracture, uncovering a unsettling fixation on absolute dominance and control. As Cam's physical recovery advances, his mental reality unravels through terrifying nightmarish visions, leaving him to question whether his idol is saving his career or orchestrating his total undoing.

story_structure.climax: The true, sinister nature of Isaiah's motives and the compound's environment comes to a head in a high-stakes confrontation, forcing Cam to fight for his mind, career, and survival.
story_structure.conflict: Cam arrives at the compound eager to rebuild his career, but struggles to balance the intense physical and mental demands of the elite training regimen with the unsettling atmosphere surrounding Isaiah and his celebrity lifestyle.
story_structure.resolution: The ordeal reaches a definitive conclusion as Cam is forced to reconcile his ambitions with the hidden costs of reaching the top, irrevocably altered by his time at the compound.
story_structure.introduction: Promising athlete Cameron Cade faces the end of his career following a severe brain injury, until legendary quarterback Isaiah White invites him to train at his secluded, high-profile compound.
story_structure.risingAction: As Cam's training becomes increasingly rigorous and unconventional, Isaiah's charismatic mentorship turns psychologically intense, exposing strange dynamics and deep-seated obsession within the isolated estate.
